# Story 06 — App shell, auth flow, Arabic/English RTL

## Prerequisites

- [Story 05 completed](05-story-05-sla-kb-reports-ai-api.md), merged to `main` via `dev` (PR #8).
  **The backend is complete and frozen for this story** — no endpoint should be missing.
- [Story 01](01-story-01-foundation.md)'s frontend scaffold: Vite 6 + React 19 + TypeScript,
  Tailwind 3.4, shadcn/ui (`Button`, `Card`), React Router, TanStack Query, `src/api/client.ts`,
  i18next plumbing with `en.json`/`ar.json`.
- **Two inherited constraints, both explained in `00-overview.md`'s "Story 01 — as built" section —
  do not undo either:**
  - **Vite is pinned to 6, jsdom to 26**, because the dev machine runs Node 18. Do not
    `npm install <pkg>@latest` blindly; check the installed major version resolves on Node 18 first.
  - **`src/index.css` holds shadcn v3 HSL triplets**, not the v4 `oklch()` values the `shadcn` CLI
    generates by default. Backend Task 2 replaces this file's palette entirely with the one from
    `DesignSystem.dc.html` — keep the replacement in the same HSL-triplet shape the v3
    `tailwind.config.js` expects, or colours vanish exactly as they did in story 01.
- `docker compose exec api pytest` remains the backend test command; this story does not touch it.

---

## Story Goal

Build the shell every later screen sits inside: the API client with a real refresh flow, the
authenticated route tree, the top chrome from the design, the shared component vocabulary, and a
**complete** Arabic/English flip.

**Do the RTL work now, not at the end.** Retrofitting direction-awareness onto finished screens means
auditing every margin, every icon, every chevron. Doing it here costs one rule, held from this commit
onward: **no directional Tailwind utility anywhere in `src/`.** `ms-*`/`me-*` never `ml-*`/`mr-*`;
`ps-*`/`pe-*` never `pl-*`/`pr-*`; `text-start`/`text-end` never `text-left`/`text-right`. Hold that
and story 10's Arabic sweep is a translation pass. Break it once and every later story inherits the
same audit story 10 was designed to avoid.

**The shared components are the vocabulary stories 07–09 speak.** Their prop shapes matter more than
their visual polish — get `<StatusBadge status="escalated" />` right and stories 07–09 become
assembly, not design.

## Frontend Tasks

*(Renumbering the section as "Frontend Tasks" — everything in this story is frontend; there is no
backend work.)*

### 1 — API client: the refresh interceptor

**File: `frontend/src/api/client.ts`** — extend, do not replace `getHealth`.

```ts
// A module-level promise, not a boolean flag: every 401 arriving while a
// refresh is already in flight awaits the SAME promise rather than firing
// its own POST /auth/refresh/. Ten expired-token requests in parallel — the
// queue tab's own concurrent fetches after an idle tab — produce one refresh
// call, not ten, and one of the ten racing to invalidate the token first
// would otherwise fail the other nine.
let refreshing: Promise<string> | null = null;
```

- Request interceptor attaches `Authorization: Bearer <access>` from a small `tokenStore` (module
  state backed by `localStorage`, one get/set pair — not scattered `localStorage.getItem` calls).
- Response interceptor: on 401 from any route **other than** `auth/login/` and `auth/refresh/`
  themselves (guard by URL, or the interceptor refreshes forever on a bad login), await `refreshing`
  (creating it if unset), retry the original request once with the new token. A failed refresh clears
  `tokenStore` and redirects — **to `/login` or `/portal/login`**, chosen by the `role` cached
  alongside the token (Frontend Task 3 explains why a cached role, not a fresh `/auth/me/` call, is
  the right source here — the session is already invalid).
- `refreshing` is set to `null` in a `finally`, win or lose, so the next 401 after a successful
  refresh starts a fresh one rather than reusing a resolved promise forever.

**File: `frontend/src/api/queryKeys.ts`** (new) — one object, e.g.
`export const qk = { me: ["auth", "me"] as const, health: ["health"] as const }`, extended by every
later story rather than each inventing its own key shape. Centralising this now is what criterion 2
("query keys centralised... so invalidation cannot drift") asks for; retrofitting it after stories
07–09 have each written their own keys is real rework.

**File: `frontend/src/api/auth.ts`** (new) — typed hooks: `useLogin()` (a mutation posting
`{username, password}`, storing the token pair and the `user` payload from the response — **do not
make a second `/auth/me/` call right after login; the login response already carries it**),
`useMe()` (a query on `qk.me`, `enabled: hasToken()`), `useLogout()` (clears `tokenStore`, resets the
query client, navigates to the role-appropriate login).

### 5 — Route tree, guards, role-aware redirects

**File: `frontend/src/main.tsx`** — restructure into two layout subtrees under one router.

```
/login                          public
/portal/login                   public   (a distinct route; story 09 fills its screen — this
                                           story only needs it to exist as a redirect target)
/app        (ProtectedRoute, agentOrAbove)  → AppChrome → { /dashboard, /_kitchen-sink }
/portal     (ProtectedRoute, customerOnly)  → PortalChrome → { index: placeholder }
```

**Create file: `frontend/src/components/shell/ProtectedRoute.tsx`**

- No token → redirect to the role-appropriate login, **capturing the attempted path** in router
  state (`state={{ from: location }}`) so Frontend Task 4's post-login redirect can return to it —
  criterion 4's "preserving the intended destination."
- Token present but `useMe()` still loading → a full-screen skeleton, not a flash of the login page.
- `useMe()` resolved with the wrong role for this subtree (`customer` under `/app`,
  anything-but-`customer` under `/portal`) → redirect to the other subtree's home, **not** to login —
  criterion 5. This is a **role check, not a permission check**: it decides which app shell the user
  sees, not what they can do inside it.
- `useMe()` failing with a **401** → the interceptor already tried to refresh and lost; treat as
  logged out. Failing with anything else (network error, 500) → show a retry state, do **not** log
  the user out for a transient backend hiccup.

### 6 — Shared components

**Create `frontend/src/components/ui/` entries, each with a co-located `*.test.tsx`:**

- **`StatusBadge`** — all eight values from `backend/apps/tickets/models.py`'s `Status` choices
  (`new|open|pending|on_hold|escalated|resolved|closed|reopened`), bilingual label via `t()`, colour
  per `DesignSystem.dc.html`'s status swatch row.
- **`PriorityBadge`** — `low|normal|high|urgent`, the `priority-*` Tailwind tokens from Frontend
  Task 2.
- **`ChannelBadge`** — `web|email|whatsapp|sms|chat`, each with a `lucide-react` icon matching the
  artboard's per-channel colour (`c-web`/`c-email`/`c-whatsapp`/`c-sms`/`c-chat` classes in the
  source `.dc.html` files name the exact pairing).
- **`SlaBar`** — props `{ state: "ok"|"approaching"|"breached", secondsRemaining: number,
  targetMinutes: number, policyName: string }` — **this exact shape is what story 05's
  `response_sla`/`resolution_sla` already returns**, so story 07 passes the API response straight in
  with no adapter. Renders a progress bar plus "2h left" or "Breached 14m" derived from the **signed**
  `secondsRemaining` (negative = breached), and **ticks live via its own `setInterval`, scoped to the
  component** (not a page-level re-render) — the story's stated performance requirement. Unmount
  clears the interval.
- **`EmptyState`**, **`Skeleton`**, **`ConfirmDialog`** (wraps shadcn `AlertDialog`), and a toast
  helper (`npx shadcn@latest add toast` and a `useToast` re-export, or `sonner` if the shadcn toast
  primitive proves fiddly under React 19 — either is fine, but pick **one** and note the choice in
  the journal so stories 07–09 don't introduce a second).
- **`DataTable`** — sortable columns (controlled sort state, not client re-sorting a server page —
  it exposes an `onSortChange` the caller wires to its query), pagination controls, a loading
  skeleton row set, an empty state, and **RTL-aware** column alignment (`text-start`, never
  `text-left`). Generic over row type (`DataTable<T>`); story 07 is its first real consumer.

Every component's visible text is a translation key — criterion 8. Extend `en.json`/`ar.json` with
only the keys this story's own components and screens use (`nav.*`, `auth.*`, `status.*`,
`priority.*`, `channel.*`, `sla.*`) — **not** keys for tickets/customers/KB screens that do not exist
yet; the intake says translate what renders, not pre-populate for later stories.

### 7 — i18n and the RTL flip

**File: `frontend/src/i18n/index.ts`** — read the persisted language on init
(`localStorage.getItem("lang")`), falling back to the browser default, falling back to `"en"`.

**File: `frontend/src/components/shell/LanguageToggle.tsx`** — on change: `i18n.changeLanguage()`,
set `document.documentElement.lang` and `document.documentElement.dir`
(`ar` → `rtl`, else `ltr`), persist to `localStorage`. **On first load after login**, if no language
is yet persisted, apply `useMe()`'s `language` field once — criterion 9's "applies the logged-in
user's language field on first load" — and only then, so a returning user's explicit toggle choice is
never overridden by their profile default.

**Numerals stay Western (0–9) in both languages** — do not let `Intl.NumberFormat` localise digits;
pin the locale used for numbers to `"en"` regardless of UI language, per the design.

**Create file: `frontend/src/lib/format.ts`** — one shared date/duration formatter
(`Intl.DateTimeFormat` keyed off the active `i18n.language`, numerals pinned as above). Every screen
imports from here; nothing calls `Intl.DateTimeFormat` inline. This is "the choice is made once."

**The CI-runnable RTL guard — criterion 11:**

**Create file: `frontend/scripts/check-rtl.mjs`**
```js
// Fails the build on a directional Tailwind utility anywhere in src/. Run via
// `npm run check:rtl`, and from CI / the story-10 sweep. A regex over class
// strings, not a linter plugin — zero new dependencies, and precise enough
// for the exact class list the intake names.
```
Grep-equivalent over `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` for the exact tokens the intake lists:
`\bml-`, `\bmr-`, `\bpl-`, `\bpr-`, `text-left`, `text-right`, `\bleft-`, `\bright-` (word-boundary
anchored so `text-left` doesn't false-positive on something like `content-left-align` if that ever
appears, and `left-` doesn't match `flex-1`-style utilities). Exit 1 and print every match with its
file and line. Add `"check:rtl": "node scripts/check-rtl.mjs"` to `package.json` scripts, and run it
in Backend Task 8's verification — every subsequent story's plan should call it too.

### 8 — Kitchen sink and tests

**Create file: `frontend/src/routes/KitchenSink.tsx`**, routed at `/app/_kitchen-sink` **inside**
`AppChrome`'s protected tree (so it's reachable while logged in, not a stray public route) — every
shared component in every documented state (`StatusBadge` × 8, `PriorityBadge` × 4, `ChannelBadge` ×
5, `SlaBar` × 3 states, `DataTable` empty/loading/populated, both toggle languages side by side via a
local in-page switcher). **Exclude it from the production build** via a Vite `define` flag checked at
router-construction time (`import.meta.env.DEV` gate, or a `VITE_KITCHEN_SINK` env var) — not a
runtime role check, which would still ship the code.

**Tests** (Vitest + Testing Library, matching `Login.test.tsx`'s existing style):
- Each shared component: one test per documented state exists and renders the right text/class.
- `ProtectedRoute`: unauthenticated → redirect with preserved `from`; wrong role → redirect to the
  other subtree; loading → skeleton, not a flash of login.
- The refresh interceptor: **the concurrent-401 case** — fire two calls against a mocked 401 response
  and assert exactly one `POST /auth/refresh/` occurs (mock `axios`/`msw`; this is criterion 1's
  "concurrent 401s share a single refresh" and the one most likely to be silently wrong without a
  test forcing the race).
- `LanguageToggle`: sets `dir`/`lang` on `document.documentElement`, persists, and does not override
  an already-persisted choice with `useMe()`'s language.
- `SlaBar`: renders "Breached" styling for negative `secondsRemaining`, ticks the displayed value
  after advancing fake timers, and clears its interval on unmount (assert via a spy, not a leak
  detector).

## Verification Steps

1. **`npm run check:rtl`** — exits 0 against this story's own code.
2. **Login round-trip against the real API:**
   ```bash
   docker compose up -d
   cd frontend && npm run dev
   ```
   Open `http://localhost:5173/login`, sign in as `agent@demo` / `Demo!2345`, land on
   `/app/dashboard` with the chrome rendered and the existing health card still visible.
3. **Role redirects:** log in as `customer@demo` → lands on `/portal`, not `/app/dashboard`.
   Manually navigate to `/app/dashboard` while still authenticated as the customer → bounced to
   `/portal`. Log out, hit `/app/dashboard` directly → bounced to `/login`, and completing that login
   returns to `/app/dashboard` (the preserved destination).
4. **Refresh survives an expired token:** in devtools, edit the stored access token to garbage,
   trigger a request (reload `/app/dashboard`) — one call to `/auth/refresh/` in the network tab,
   then the original request replays and succeeds.
5. **Arabic is total:** toggle to `ع` — chrome, nav labels, search placeholder and every kitchen-sink
   label flip to Arabic, the page direction is `rtl`, the sidebar/chrome mirrors, and a ticket number
   or phone number rendered anywhere stays left-to-right inside the Arabic text.
6. **Kitchen sink:** `/app/_kitchen-sink` renders every component/state pair correctly in both
   languages; confirm it is absent from `npm run build`'s output bundle (grep `dist/` for a
   kitchen-sink-only string and find nothing).
7. **Tests:** `npm run test -- --run` — all green, including the concurrent-401 interceptor test and
   the `SlaBar` timer test.
8. **Build:** `npm run build` exits 0.
9. **Regression:** `docker compose exec api pytest -q` still green (untouched by this story, but
   confirms nothing in `.env`/CORS broke the container wiring); `/api/v1/health/`, `/schema/`,
   `/docs/` still reachable.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] `src/api/client.ts` refreshes once on 401, shares a single in-flight refresh across concurrent
      401s, retries the original request, and redirects to the correct login on a failed refresh.
- [ ] Typed hooks in `src/api/` (`useLogin`, `useMe`, `useLogout`, plus `getHealth` preserved) with
      query keys centralised in `src/api/queryKeys.ts`.
- [ ] `/login`: react-hook-form + zod, inline errors, a readable failure message, a loading and
      double-submit-proof submit button, correct demo-credential hints.
- [ ] `ProtectedRoute` redirects unauthenticated users to the right login preserving the intended
      destination, and returns them there after success.
- [ ] Role-aware redirects both directions: customer on `/app/*` → `/portal`; agent-or-above on
      `/portal/*` → `/app/dashboard`.
- [ ] `AppChrome` matches `Main.dc.html`: lockup, nav, search (inert this story), language toggle,
      user chip with profile/sign-out menu, `Admin` linking to `/admin/` for admins only.
- [ ] Nav items the current role cannot reach are **not rendered**.
- [ ] i18next with `en.json`/`ar.json`; every visible string in this story's own components is a
      translation key.
- [ ] Language toggle sets `dir`/`lang` on `<html>`, persists, and applies the profile default only
      when nothing is yet persisted.
- [ ] Arabic flips completely — chrome included — with numerals staying Western and dates through
      one shared formatter.
- [ ] `npm run check:rtl` exists, runs in CI-style verification, and fails on any of the eight listed
      directional-utility patterns.
- [ ] `StatusBadge`, `PriorityBadge`, `ChannelBadge`, `SlaBar`, `EmptyState`, `Skeleton`,
      `ConfirmDialog`, a toast helper, and `DataTable` all exist under `src/components/ui/`, each
      with a passing test. `SlaBar`'s prop shape matches `response_sla`/`resolution_sla` verbatim.
- [ ] `/app/_kitchen-sink` renders every component/state in both languages and is absent from the
      production bundle.
- [ ] **Entry appended to `docs/AI_USAGE.md`** with elapsed time, noting the toast-library choice and
      that the search field is inert until story 07.
- [ ] `.squad/plans/crm-mvp/00-overview.md` updated with this story **and its own "as built" section**
      following the pattern stories 01–05 established, since story 07 will need to read it the same
      way this plan read story 05's.
